hyps.why: With edge 1 already a strong 3x3 conv, adding a 3x3 conv on edge 2 gives diminishing returns (about 0 versus +2 to +4 otherwise).
When edge 0 is none the skip on edge 3 restores an input path to the output, giving a much larger gain.
A skip on edge 0 already supplies cheap identity-like paths, so another skip on edge 3 adds little.
Replacing a missing edge with a 3x3 conv adds an entire learnable path, whereas replacing an existing op yields a smaller gain.
Redundant 3x3 capacity on the parallel direct edge 3 reduces the marginal value of upgrading edge 0.
Stacking parameter-free pooling on both the 0->2 and 2->3 routes sharply loses representational capacity.
With a skip on edge 5 the node-2 route has little learnable capacity, so pooling edge 1 hurts more.
Removing a redundant skip can help, while removing a learned 3x3 conv on edge 5 hurts.
Replacing a pooling op with an identity skip is beneficial, while replacing a 3x3 conv with a skip is harmful.
Adding a skip where the edge was absent is a pure gain, while replacing a conv or pool with a skip loses capacity.
